intro.text: The calmest skill: click a tree and the character chops until the inventory is full. Good for the background.

items.text: **Chopping in company.** Since the Forestry update every player chopping the same tree gives a hidden +1 level bonus (up to +10), and trees disappear on a timer, no faster. So on the busy Draynor willows chopping pays better.
**Forestry events.** With a Forestry kit on free worlds the events Struggling sapling, Rising roots and Friendly ent happen. They give more XP and bark for a valuable axe handle.
**Danger at the Draynor willows:** dark wizards (level 7) wander nearby and can attack a very weak character.
**Inventory full?** For XP drop the logs (shift + click), for money bank them. The Draynor willows have a bank next to them, so there is almost no difference.
**The character stopped chopping.** The tree has disappeared for a while; move to a neighbouring one.
**Where do I get a better axe?** The Grand Exchange or the axe shop Bob's Brilliant Axes in Lumbridge (up to steel).
**With membership:** tick methods, redwoods, magic trees and the Woodcutting Guild.

intro.text: Fires are trained quickly and without risk: you need a tinderbox (Tinderbox) and logs, your own or bought.

items.text: Take a tinderbox and 27 logs from the bank.
Stand at the start of an empty straight line: the rows by the Grand Exchange in Varrock are the most convenient, with a bank next to them.
Use the tinderbox on a log. After the fire the character steps west by itself, and the next fire lines up.
When the logs run out go back to the bank and start a new line.

blocks.text: A calm option: while chopping, light a Forester's campfire by the tree and feed it logs. Less XP, but almost no clicks.

items.text: **"You can't light a fire here".** There is already a fire on this tile or lighting one is not allowed. Step to a neighbouring empty tile.
**Where is the tinderbox?** The Lumbridge General Store.
**Why fires?** You can cook on them anywhere. With membership the Wintertodt minigame opens at level 50.

intro.text: Fishing feeds all your combat: you cook the fish you catch and carry it as food. Fishing spots are marked with a light-blue fish icon, and the Fishing plugin highlights them.

blocks.text: On the Port Sarim dock talk to the sailors and pay 30 coins. To come back, use the Customs officer on Karamja, also 30 coins. There is no bank on the island: the catch is put in the deposit box on the Port Sarim dock. What to answer the sailors and the customs officer is in the section [Teleports, canoes and boats](#/reference/transport).

items.text: **Where do I get tackle?** The fishing shop Gerrant's Fishy Business in Port Sarim: nets, rods, feathers, bait, pots, harpoons.
**The fishing spot is gone.** Spots sometimes move; look for the fish icon nearby.
**Drop or cook?** For Fishing XP drop it. For food cook it yourself, which trains Cooking as well.
**With membership:** barbarian fishing, sharks, the Fishing Guild.

intro.text: Cook usable catches at your observed Cooking level. The Plan checks recipe unlocks, burning, supplies and budget; Fishing does not guarantee matching Cooking progress.

sections.title: How to cook a lot at once

items.text: Take 28 raw fish from the bank.
Use the fish on a range (Range) and choose "All": the character cooks the whole inventory by itself.
Take it to the bank and repeat.

**Why does food burn?** The chance to burn drops with level and is lower on a range than on a fire. It burns least on the range in the Lumbridge Castle kitchen, but only for simple food and only after the quest Cook's Assistant.
**Al Kharid.** After the quest Prince Ali Rescue the gate is free. The bank and the range are a couple of steps from each other.
**How much food to take into combat?** As much as fits after the gear: usually 15–20 pieces of the best fish you can cook.
**With membership:** monkfish, karambwans, sharks and ranges right next to a bank.

intro.text: Mining is the basis of Smithing: you smelt bars from your own ore and forge weapons and armour.

head: Level
Ore
XP
What for
rows: Iron and steel, the best XP

blocks.text: Stand so that 2–3 iron rocks are next to you. Mine them in a circle: while one recovers you mine another. When the inventory is full drop the ore (shift + click). This is the fastest Mining XP in the free version.

items.text: **What kind of rock is it?** Hover the cursor: the name says which ore it is. An empty rock is grey and will recover soon.
**Camdozaal** is the underground mines after Below Ice Mountain. From Mining 14 you mine Barronite there: slowly, but very calmly, and a little Smithing XP drips in along the way.
**Runite ore (Runite, 85)** in the free version is only in the Wilderness, which is dangerous.
**With membership:** the Motherlode Mine, AFK mining with good XP, gems, and a guild with a wide choice of ore.

intro.text: Smelt bars in a furnace and forge items on an anvil with a hammer. Use Train for a recipe matched to your levels, supplies and budget; a higher-level recipe is not automatically the best choice.

items.text: **Furnace:** Edgeville is the nearest to a bank in the free version. There are also ones in Al Kharid, Falador and Lumbridge.
**Anvil:** south of the west Varrock bank, the nearest to a bank.

head: Bar
Level
Ore
XP per smelt
rows: 1 iron, comes out in about half the cases

blocks.text: Each metal has a base level: bronze 1, iron 15, steel 30, mithril 50, adamant 70, rune 85. An item's level = the base + the bonus from the table.

items.text: **The iron did not smelt.** In the free version an iron bar comes out in about half the cases, and the ore is lost on a failure. The spell Superheat Item (Magic 43) always smelts iron.
**Is your own cheaper than bought?** Usually not: ready-made armour on the GE is often cheaper than the bars. You make your own for XP and fun.
**A calm option.** Smelting bars in Edgeville is almost AFK and sometimes even at a profit. Check the GE prices before you start.
**With membership:** the Blast Furnace and cannonballs (AFK smithing).

intro.text: Leather armour for an archer, pottery, gem cutting and jewellery. The tools, a needle (Needle), thread (Thread), a chisel (Chisel) and moulds (Mould), are sold in the crafting shop Rommik's Crafty Supplies in Rimmington.

blocks.text: Cowhides (Cowhide) drop from the cows by Lumbridge. Have them tanned by the tanner Ellis in Al Kharid (1 coin for soft leather, 3 for hard) and use a needle on the leather. Thread is used up little by little, so take a spool with a margin.
A ring, necklace or amulet with a gem is made at a furnace: a gold bar + a cut gem + a mould. The sapphire ring is from level 20, the emerald from 27, the ruby from 34, the diamond from 43.

In Barbarian Village there are a pottery wheel and an oven. Wet clay (Clay) with water to get soft clay (Soft clay). On the wheel: a pot (1), a pie dish (7), a bowl (8). An Unfired bowl is needed for Dragon Slayer I.

items.text: **Out of hides?** The cows east of Lumbridge are an endless source, and you train combat along the way.
**The Crafting Guild** west of Falador opens at Crafting 40 and needs a Brown apron. Inside are gold, clay and a bank.
**The most expensive part of Crafting** is the gems from the GE. The cheapest way to train is on leather, if you collect the hides yourself.
**With membership:** dragonhide, glassblowing, battlestaves.

title: Melee combat: Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints
name: Melee combat

intro.text: For every point of damage you get 4 XP in the skill of the chosen style and about 1.3 Hitpoints XP. The style is chosen in the tab with the sword (Combat Options).

head: Style
What it trains
rows: Attack: accuracy and access to better weapons
Defence: access to better armour, you are hit less often
All three a little (not on every weapon)

intro.text: Use Train for an order matched to your current goal, equipment, supplies and budget. There is no fixed Attack, Strength and Defence order for every account.

head: Metal
Attack (weapon)
Defence (armour)
rows: 40 (the platebody only after Dragon Slayer I)

items.text: **For training** use a scimitar (Scimitar): fast and accurate. A rune scimitar from Attack 40 will serve the whole free game.
**Against dragons** use a rune shortsword (Rune shortsword): a stab attack, and Elvarg is weak to it.
**Against demons** use Silverlight from the quest Demon Slayer.
**How much food to take?** 10–15 pieces of the best fish you can cook. Eat when your health is below half.
**Is the monster too strong?** The colour of the level above it: green and yellow are fine, red is too early.
**The monsters stopped attacking on their own.** Aggressive monsters calm down after 10 minutes in one place. Step far away and come back.
**Auto retaliate.** Turn on Auto Retaliate in the combat tab so the character answers attacks by itself.
**Hitpoints** do not need training separately: it grows by itself in any combat.

subtitle: Attack, Strength, Defence, Hitpoints

intro.text: Ranged attacks can be used from a safespot where the target cannot reach you. The training plan checks your level, equipment and supplies, and directs you to an available shop or the Grand Exchange when something is needed.

blocks.text: Armour: leather from 1 (you can sew it yourself, see "Crafting"), a hard leather body from Defence 10, green dragonhide (Green d'hide) from Ranged 40; the body only after Dragon Slayer I.

head: Style
What it gives
rows: More accurate, all the XP to Ranged
Trains Ranged; use the current plan for the selected setup.
Shoots farther, the XP is split between Ranged and Defence

items.text: **Running out of arrows?** Some arrows fall on the ground next to the monster: pick them up, the Ground Items plugin highlights them.
**Combine with melee?** Yes, the skills are independent. It is convenient to train them in turn when you get tired of one.
**For Dragon Slayer I** a bow does not work: you need a shield against dragonfire, and a bow is two-handed. Melee is better against dragons.

intro.text: Combat spells, teleports and useful enchantments. Every spell uses runes: the basic ones are sold by the mage Aubury in Varrock and Betty in Port Sarim, the rest on the GE. An elemental staff (Staff of air, fire and so on) replaces the runes of its element: the staff shop of Zaff in Varrock.

head: Level
Spell
XP
What for
rows: A sapphire amulet into an Amulet of magic
Pick up an item from afar (one way to the Wormbrain map piece in Dragon Slayer I)
A bar from ore without a furnace, iron always succeeds
An item into gold pays better

items.text: **Does armour hinder magic?** Yes, metal lowers spell accuracy. A mage is better in robes (Wizard robe).
**An efficient trick:** from 55 and up you can turn forged platebodies into gold with High Level Alchemy on the way between the anvil and the bank.
**With membership:** ancient spells, the lunar book, arceuus spells.

intro.text: Prayer gives temporary boosts in combat. You train it by burying bones (click a bone, Bury) and with XP lamps from quests. Prayer points are restored at an altar (Altar), for example in Lumbridge church.

head: Bone
XP
Where from
rows: Almost any monsters: chickens, cows, goblins
Giant frogs, hill, moss and ice giants
Brutus, after The Ides of Milk (bury only)

Prayer
What it gives
rows: Thick Skin, Rock Skin, Steel Skin
Burst of Strength, Superhuman Strength, Ultimate Strength
Clarity of Thought, Improved Reflexes, Incredible Reflexes
Sharp Eye, Hawk Eye, Eagle Eye
Mystic Will, Mystic Lore, Mystic Might
After death 1 more item is kept
Protection from magic, missiles and melee

items.text: **Prayer runs out fast.** Turn it on only against hard monsters and turn it off right after the fight.
**Bury or sell big bones?** Up to Prayer 43 it is better to bury them: Protect from Melee makes combat much easier.
**With membership:** an altar in your own house and temples give 3.5 times more XP per bone.

intro.text: Your own runes for magic. It opens with the quest **Rune Mysteries** (step S2-06). After it the mage Aubury in Varrock teleports you to the rune essence mine (Rune essence).

**How it works:** you mine essence in Aubury's mine, carry it to the altar of the element you want with a talisman (Talisman) or a tiara (Tiara), enter the altar and use the essence on the altar inside. As your level grows one essence gives more runes: for example, air runes come 2 at a time from level 11.

items.text: **Slow?** Yes, in the free version it is one of the slowest skills. Train it when you need your own runes or fancy a calm run around.
**Where do I get a talisman?** Rune Mysteries gives the air talisman, and the others drop from monsters or are sold on the GE.
**A tiara** takes no inventory space: it is made from a silver bar with a mould (Crafting 23) and bound to a talisman at the altar.
**With membership:** the Guardians of the Rift minigame is the most popular way to train runes.
